title: ODI knowledge base
description: One JSON file holding an Outcome-Driven Innovation study built from interview transcripts. Made with Product Weaver · productweaver.com. It covers schema versions 3 and 4 (`meta.schema_version`). Extra fields are allowed so older and derived layers keep loading; the fields below are the contract.

language.description: The study's language, a BCP 47 code such as en, it, pt-BR or zh-Hans. Every statement is written in it, and so are the map's and the review sheet's own text. Missing means English. Set by init or labels, before the first interview.

tool_version.description: Computed. Version of kb_tool.py that last wrote the file.

style.description: Optional writing rules for this study. Each key overrides the script's default.

limits.description: Maximum words per kind of statement: executor, job, step, outcome, feeling, rationale, solution, group.

banned.description: Tokens a statement may not contain.

idioms.description: Phrases with and/or that are one idea, such as bread and butter.

acronyms.description: Abbreviations every reviewer in this market knows.

directions.description: How a new outcome must start, such as Ridurre al minimo. Default in an English study: Minimize, Maximize, Increase, Reduce; elsewhere none is checked.

need_start.description: How a value theme's need must start, such as Aiutami a. Default in an English study: Help me; elsewhere none is checked.

core_jobs.description: The core functional jobs this study found, abstracted from each interview's own core job.

interviews.description: Computed. Interviews whose own core job rolls up to this one.

related_interviews.description: Computed. Interviews with a related job that rolls up to this one.

coverage.description: Computed. Interviews quoted on this job's steps or outcomes.

clusters.description: Segments, keyed by a short code.

interactions.description: Each later conversation with the same person, numbered from 2 in the order added. The record's own file, sha256, date and format are the first conversation.

id.description: Computed. Job letter and number, such as A.6.

n.description: Step number inside its core job. Stable once published.

voices.description: Computed. Distinct people quoted on the step or on any of its outcomes.

statement.description: Direction, metric, object and context. In an English study it starts with Minimize, Maximize, Increase or Reduce; the merge checks the opening, which depends on meta.language.

current_solutions.description: What people use today to get a step done, and what they stopped using. Optional: the first merge that adds a solution creates it.

groups.description: Groups of solutions that compete for the same work, keyed by a short lowercase key.

why.description: Why these solutions belong together, in one sentence.

solutions.description: Computed: the live solutions in this group.

interviews.description: Computed: who is quoted on a current use.

stopped_by.description: Computed: who is quoted only on stopped uses.

quote_count.description: Computed: how many different quotes mention it.

target.description: Step ID for reword_step and move_step; outcome ID for reword_outcome, merge_outcomes and move_outcome; core job ID for reword_core_job and confirm_core_job; segment key for new_segment; interview ID for relink_interview; solution ID for merge_solutions, move_solution and reword_solution; group key for reword_solution_group.

merge.description: merge_outcomes: the outcome folded into target. merge_solutions: the solution folded into target.

to_group.description: move_solution: the group the solution moves to.

why.description: reword_solution_group: the group's new reason, one sentence.

job.description: new_step: the core job the step joins. relink_interview: the core job to link to, or null.

steps.description: new_core_job: the new job's first steps, numbered from 1 when it is approved.

interviews.description: new_core_job: interviews whose own core job is linked to the new job when it is approved.

related_job.description: relink_interview: the related job to link, by its statement. Without it, the main link changes.

ts.description: When the script wrote this entry, ISO 8601 with timezone. Hand-written entries may leave it out.

run_id.description: The run that wrote this entry. The same value is on its line in logs/kb_tool.jsonl, so the entry can be traced to its log line and backup.

added_interviews.description: merge: IDs of the interviews added.

added_interactions.description: merge: the later conversations added, each as its person's interview ID and its number. Present only when there are some.

new_outcomes.description: merge: IDs of the outcomes added.

new_solutions.description: merge: IDs of the solutions added.

new_solution_groups.description: merge: keys of the solution groups added.

solution_quotes.description: merge: quotes added to solutions already in the KB.

proposals.description: merge: IDs of the proposals filed.

bootstrap.description: merge: true when this merge created the core jobs and job map.

layer.description: rebuild: the derived layer that was rebuilt, such as value_themes.

job.description: rebuild: the core job whose value themes or survey were written.

themes.description: rebuild: IDs of that core job's value themes after the run.

survey.description: One survey per core job: the questions a respondent answers, worded by the assistant. Written by `kb_tool.py survey --write`. The schema types only `stale` and `stale_reasons`: a survey made by hand before 0.18 still loads. `survey --write` checks each entry it writes against `survey_job`, and refuses to write one that breaks it.

jobs.description: One survey per core job, each shaped like `survey_job`. Any other shape is allowed and ignored: only an entry with a string `job`, an integer `version` and `needs` whose every item has a string `outcome` and `text` is read as a survey.

legacy.description: What a survey made by hand before 0.18 held, kept unchanged by the first `survey --write` that met it: a list of its entries and other content. Never read.

simulation.description: The estimate: how each person of a core job would rate each need of its survey, judged from the interviews. Written by `kb_tool.py survey --estimate`. The schema types only `stale` and `stale_reasons`: an estimate made by hand before 0.18 still loads. `survey --estimate` checks each entry it writes against `simulation_job`, and refuses to write one that breaks it.

jobs.description: One estimate per core job, each shaped like `simulation_job`. Any other shape is allowed and ignored: only an entry with a string `job`, an integer `version` and `cells` whose every cell has string `interview` and `outcome`, ratings from 1 to 5 and a `basis` is read as an estimate.

legacy.description: What an estimate made by hand before 0.18 held, kept unchanged by the first `survey --estimate` that met it: a list of its entries and other content. Never read.

value_themes.description: Value themes: a few needs in the customer's words that group the desired outcomes of a core job, to sort ideas into. Written by `kb_tool.py themes`.

unassigned.description: Computed. Live outcomes that sit in no theme, for the core jobs that have themes.

overview.description: The study told as a short story for someone new to the method, one entry per core job, with what to do next. Written by `kb_tool.py overview`. The map counts unmet needs and ranks themes itself.

was_job.description: The core job an interview's job statement was linked to before; null when it had none.

was_reason.description: The unlinked_reason an interview's core job had before it was linked.

was_group.description: The group a solution was in before it moved.

was_kind.description: A solution's kind before it was corrected.

was_why.description: A solution group's reason before it was reworded.

provenance.description: Where a batch came from: which assistant and model extracted it, when that started, which interviews were read, and notes for later readers. merge: copied from the patch, with transcripts_read as KB interview IDs.

assistant.description: The AI assistant that wrote the patch, such as claude-code, codex, cursor, copilot or gemini-cli.

model.description: The model behind it, such as claude-opus-5-5.

started.description: When the assistant started reading transcripts for this batch, ISO 8601 with timezone.

transcripts_read.description: The interviews read for this batch. Never file names: they carry the interviewee's name.

notes.description: Anything a later reader should know about how this batch was extracted.

job_id.description: A core job's ID: A, B, C… then AA.

step_id.description: A step's ID: its core job's letter and its number inside that job, such as A.6.

outcome_id.description: An outcome's ID: its step's ID and its number under that step, such as A.6.3.

own_job.description: An interview's own core functional job or related job, with an optional link to a core job.

unlinked_reason.description: Core functional job only: why it rolls up to none of the study's core jobs. Leave out when job is set.

solution_id.description: A solution's ID, such as S3. Study-wide, never reused.

group_key.description: A solution group's short lowercase key, such as send-orders.

solution_kind.description: product: a product, app or service they sign up to. everyday_tool: a general tool bent to the job, such as a spreadsheet, paper or a phone. people: a person or firm who does it for them. own_method: a habit, rule of thumb or doing it in their head.

solution_status.description: current: they use it now. stopped: they used it for this step and stopped; the quote usually says why.

solution_use.description: One step a solution is used for, with the quotes that show it. One per step and status.

value_theme.description: One value theme. A theme with no id was written by hand before `kb_tool.py themes` existed; the script keeps it and does not check it.

label.description: Verb-first name of at most 6 words.

need.description: The need in the customer's voice: one sentence that starts with 'Help me' in an English study, or the same request in the study's language, at most 25 words.

why.description: What binds the outcomes, in one sentence of at most 30 words.

outcomes.description: IDs of the outcomes the theme groups. An outcome may sit in two themes.

highlight.description: A quote picked to show a theme's pain, struggle or desire. It is a copy of a quote on one of the theme's outcomes or on a solution used at their steps.

overview_quote.description: A quote the KB already holds for the core job.

overview_job.description: One core job's overview. `kb_tool.py overview` has written every required field since the layer began; `executor` came with 0.9.0, so an older overview has none.

label.description: A short name for the people the study is about, such as "Small-firm bookkeeper".

text.description: Who they are and what they do, in one sentence.

icon.description: The icon the map draws for them; person when none fits.

others.description: Optional. Up to 3 other people who appear in the story but are not its focus.

executor.description: Who the study is about. Optional, because overviews written before it existed have none.

bottom_line.description: The main finding, in one sentence.

why.description: Why the problem is still there.

answer.description: The answer to the step's question, in one sentence.

text.description: Optional. One or two sentences that explain the answer.

answer.description: The answer to the step's question, in one sentence.

text.description: Optional. One or two sentences that explain the answer.

today.description: How they get the job done today.

answer.description: The answer to the step's question, in one sentence.

text.description: Optional. One or two sentences that explain the answer.

needs.description: What they most want to get better. The list is counted by the map.

answer.description: The answer to the step's question, in one sentence.

text.description: Optional. One or two sentences that explain the answer.

focus.description: Where a new solution should focus. The themes are ranked by the map.

next.description: What to do next, in three tracks: advice, not findings.

action.description: The one thing to do, as an instruction.

words.description: Customers' own words to reuse, each part of a quote in the KB.

traits.description: The plan's 2 or 3 people traits. A value with no interviews is a kind of person not heard yet.

rests_on.description: Outcome IDs the main finding rests on.

round.description: Who to talk to next, in order, and what to ask them.

kind.description: new: people still to find (count, who, traits). follow_up: ask someone in the study again (interview).

interview.description: follow_up only: the person to ask again.

at_write.description: Computed. The round's targets and the people heard when this plan was written.

previous.description: Computed. at_write of the plan before the last batch, to say how that round went.

action.description: The one thing to do, as an instruction.

words.description: Customers' own words to reuse, each part of a quote in the KB.

action.description: The one thing to do, as an instruction.

words.description: Customers' own words to reuse, each part of a quote in the KB.

written.description: Computed. Date the overview was written.

survey_job.description: One core job's survey, as `survey --write` writes it. The schema does not apply it to `survey.jobs`, so a hand-made survey from 0.17 still loads.

version.description: Goes up by 1 when the words a respondent reads change.

frame.description: One line shown on every step, such as "Think of a typical client and a typical month."

survey_gate.description: The check question made from the core job. "No" ends the survey there.

text.description: The question, such as "Do you close clients' books each month?"

yes.description: The words of the yes answer.

no.description: The words of the no answer.

explain.description: What "Explain" shows: one sentence of at most 25 words.

survey_question.description: One question about the person, made from a people trait of the plan.

trait.description: The trait of `overview.jobs[].next.learn.traits`, such as T1.

text.description: The question, such as "Do you work alone or in a firm?"

other.description: The words of the last choice, such as "Something else".

explain.description: What "Explain" shows: one sentence of at most 25 words.

value.description: The trait value, such as T1.2.

label.description: The choice as the respondent reads it.

survey_need.description: One need the survey asks about.

text.description: The need as the respondent reads it, starting with a verb. At most 160 characters.

explain.description: What "Explain" shows: one sentence of at most 25 words.

simulation_job.description: One core job's estimate, as `survey --estimate` writes it. The schema does not apply it to `simulation.jobs`, so a hand-made estimate from 0.17 still loads.

version.description: The version of the survey whose needs were rated.

simulation_cell.description: How one person would rate one need, and the quote it rests on.

importance.description: 1 to 5: how much the need matters to the person.

satisfaction.description: 1 to 5: how well the person's way of working today meets the need.

basis.description: said: the quote is on the need. context: it is on the need's step, or on a tool used at that step.

quote.description: The person's quote the ratings rest on, as the KB holds it.

why.description: Why these ratings, in at most 20 words.

survey_left_out.description: A live need the survey does not ask about, and why.

why.description: Why it is left out, such as "Only one person named it."
